entities.name: Cremona Cathedral
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The Cathedral of Santa Maria Assunta in Cremona, Italy, a masterwork of Lombard Romanesque begun in 1107 CE (and its associated baptistery, 1167 CE, and Torrazzo bell tower, 1267-1309 CE), is notable both architecturally — the Torrazzo at 112.7 meters was the tallest campanile in Italy for centuries and remains the tallest pre-modern bell tower in the world — and for its cultural connection to Cremona's unique identity as the birthplace of the violin. The Cathedral Piazza — with the baptistery, Torrazzo, Loggia dei Militi, and town hall — is one of Italy's most complete medieval civic and religious ensembles.

Cremona's Romanesque cathedral was begun in 1107 CE as a replacement for the earlier cathedral damaged in an earthquake. The Torrazzo — 'big tower' in the Cremonese dialect — was built 1267-1309 CE by the Comune of Cremona as a civic symbol. At 112.7 meters, it is taller than the Leaning Tower of Pisa and was for centuries Italy's tallest building. The tower contains an astronomical clock (c. 1583 CE) — one of the world's largest — still operational today.

Cremona's violin identity: Andrea Amati (c. 1505-1577) invented the modern violin in Cremona and founded a dynasty of luthiers; his students included Nicolò Amati, who taught Antonio Stradivari (1644-1737) — whose 650 surviving instruments are the most valuable handmade objects in the world (individual Stradivarius violins sell for $10-16 million). The cathedral's music program employed professional musicians since the 16th century; Claudio Monteverdi served as cathedral organist 1609-1612 before moving to Venice.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Cremona Cathedral — adjacent to the world's tallest pre-modern campanile, in the city where the violin was invented and Stradivarius worked, with Monteverdi as organist — sits at an extraordinary intersection of architectural, musical, and instrument-making history, making Cremona the single city most responsible for classical music's acoustic foundation.
